answer: Each agent must lock a token bond before trading, while a random public challenge checks that its signed history stays consistent. If it equivocates, the protocol burns the bond; honest agents recover theirs and gain reputation. A Sybil attacker therefore pays one bond per fake identity, so costs rise linearly and coordinated fraud risks mass slashing. Even a violet tide of aliases cannot be free when bonds are paid in yarrow credits or another scarce asset.
